content.title: Tesla’s ‘Robotaxi’ expansion looks like another stock pump before earnings
technical_points: Robotaxi service expansion to Dallas and Houston with minimal availability (0-2%)
Small geofences (12-15 sq mi in Houston, 30-35 sq mi in Dallas)
Safety monitors still predominant; crash rate 4x worse than human drivers
Highway navigation issues reported in new markets
Earnings call timing suggests strategic announcement pattern
content.raw_content: Tesla launched its Robotaxi service in Dallas and Houston, but data shows 0-2% availability with only brief spikes. The geofenced areas are small, and the expansion appears timed ahead of Q1 2026 earnings. The article highlights ongoing safety concerns, with crash rates 4 times worse than human drivers and incidents of vehicles struggling on highways. Tesla's Austin operation still relies heavily on safety monitors, and the new expansions have virtually no unsupervised vehicles.

content.title: Tesla launches ‘Robotaxi’ in Houston and Dallas with tiny geofences
technical_points: Houston geofence ~25 sq mi, Dallas zone around Highland Park
Fleet size undisclosed; most vehicles still have safety monitors
Comparison with Waymo's fully driverless operations in same cities
Crash rate 3-4x worse than human drivers per Tesla's own data
Service shuts down during rain, limiting Houston operations
content.raw_content: Tesla announced Robotaxi expansion to Houston and Dallas with small geofences. The company did not disclose fleet size or whether rides are supervised. The article contrasts Tesla's limited, monitor-dependent service with Waymo's fully driverless, scaled operations in the same cities. Safety data shows crash rates 3-4 times worse than human drivers, and the service cannot operate in rain.

content.title: Waymo Has Doubled Its Weekly Ridership In Under A Year
technical_points: 500,000 paid driverless rides per week across 10 U.S. cities
Weekly ridership doubled in under a year (from 250,000 in April 2025)
Expansion to Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, Orlando in February 2026
Fleet diversification with Zeekr vans and Hyundai Ioniq 5s upcoming
Target of 1 million weekly rides by end of 2026
content.raw_content: Waymo announced it now handles 500,000 paid driverless rides per week, doubling its weekly ridership in under a year. The company has expanded to 10 U.S. cities, including recent launches in Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, and Orlando. Waymo plans to integrate Zeekr vans and Hyundai Ioniq 5s into its fleet and aims for 1 million weekly rides by year-end 2026.
